question: A 26-week patient presents for re-evaluation of a 3mm perimembranous VSD. A complete fetal echocardiogram (CPT 76825/76827) was performed at 20 weeks. If 2D segmental sweeps, spectral Doppler tracings, and color flow mapping are archived today, which CPT code combination is most appropriate?
options: CPT 76816 alone (Follow-up OB ultrasound)
explanation: Because a baseline complete fetal echocardiogram (76825/76827) is already documented on record for the current pregnancy, subsequent focused cardiovascular evaluations qualify as follow-up fetal echocardiography. When 2D anatomy, spectral Doppler waveforms, and color flow velocity mapping are all performed and archived, the compliant billing triad is CPT 76826 (2D follow-up) + CPT 76828 (spectral Doppler follow-up) + CPT 93325 (color mapping add-on).
reference: SMFM Coding White Paper; ASE 2023 Guidelines

question: A 30-week patient is referred to your MFM clinic after a community anatomy scan suspected Tetralogy of Fallot. No prior fetal echocardiogram has ever been performed. The MFM specialist performs a comprehensive cardiac evaluation including 2D sweeps, spectral Doppler, and color mapping. How should this study be coded?
options: CPT 76826 + 76828 + 93325 (Follow-up echo triad)
CPT 76825 + 76827 + 93325 (Complete echo triad)
CPT 76811 + 76826 (Detailed anatomy + follow-up echo)
CPT 76816 + 93325 (Follow-up OB + color Doppler)
explanation: Follow-up fetal echocardiography codes (76826/76828) strictly require a documented prior complete study (76825/76827). When a fetus presents for its FIRST comprehensive cardiovascular assessment, it must be billed as a Complete Fetal Echocardiogram (76825 + 76827 + 93325), which establishes the baseline for any future follow-up studies in this pregnancy.
reference: SMFM Required Components for Coding Fetal Echocardiograms; AMA CPT Manual

question: During a follow-up fetal echo for pulmonary valve stenosis, the sonographer saves high-resolution 2D cine loops and color Doppler sweeps showing turbulence at the RVOT, but does NOT obtain or save any pulsed-wave or continuous-wave spectral Doppler velocity tracings. What is the coding consequence?
options: Bill 76826 + 76828 + 93325 anyway since color flow reflects hemodynamics
Bill only CPT 76826 and CPT 93325; CPT 76828 must be omitted
Bill CPT 76816 instead because spectral Doppler is mandatory for all fetal echo codes
Bill CPT 76828 alone as an unbundled hemodynamic service
explanation: CPT 76828 specifically captures spectral Doppler echocardiography (pulsed wave and/or continuous wave with spectral display). If measured velocity waveforms (e.g., peak systolic velocities, gradients, inflow profiles) are not archived in PACS, 76828 cannot be unbundled or billed. In this scenario, the compliant drop is 76826 (2D follow-up) and 93325 (color add-on).

question: An MFM physician performs a growth ultrasound with amniotic fluid index for fetal growth restriction (FGR) and, during the same visit, performs a focused follow-up fetal echocardiogram for established cardiomyopathy. How should the billing encounter be structured?
options: Bill 76816 alone, as payers automatically bundle cardiac scans into obstetric follow-ups
Bill 76826 + 76828 + 93325 and append Modifier 59 (or XE) to CPT 76816
Bill 76826 + 76828 + 93325 and append Modifier 59 to CPT 76826
Bill 76811 with Modifier 22 for increased procedural complexity
explanation: When an obstetric ultrasound (76816) and a follow-up fetal echocardiogram (76826/76828/93325) are performed on the same day for distinct medical indications, both are reimbursable. To bypass NCCI bundling edits, Modifier 59 (or Medicare XE for separate encounter) must be appended to the secondary non-cardiac procedure code (76816), supported by discrete documentation.
reference: ACOG Clinical Practice Update 2025; CMS NCCI Manual

question: Which statement regarding CPT 93325 (Doppler echocardiography color flow velocity mapping) is TRUE in the context of fetal echocardiography?
options: It can be billed as a standalone procedure code if only color Doppler is utilized
It is an add-on code that must always accompany a primary echo base code (76825, 76826, 76827, or 76828)
It is strictly bundled into 76826 under all payer guidelines and should never be submitted
It requires a separate pre-authorization number distinct from the primary echo code
explanation: CPT 93325 is designated by the AMA as an add-on code representing the distinct technical and cognitive work of spatial color flow velocity mapping. It cannot be billed as a standalone claim. In fetal echocardiography, SMFM and coding authorities support reporting 93325 alongside base codes (76825, 76826, 76827, 76828) when color flow mapping is performed and archived.
reference: AMA CPT Professional Edition; SMFM White Paper

question: A patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and high-titer anti-Ro/SSA antibodies presents at 21 weeks for fetal rhythm surveillance. How is the mechanical PR interval technically acquired and measured?
options: M-mode tracing of the interventricular septum during fetal movement
Simultaneous pulsed Doppler of mitral inflow and aortic outflow, measured from the onset of the mitral A wave to the onset of the aortic V wave
Continuous-wave Doppler of the umbilical artery measuring systolic-to-diastolic ratio
Color Doppler velocity mapping of the ductus venosus
explanation: The fetal mechanical PR interval is obtained using simultaneous pulsed-wave Doppler interrogation of left ventricular inflow (mitral valve) and outflow (ascending aorta) or SVC/ascending aorta. Calipers are placed from the onset of atrial contraction (mitral A wave) to the onset of ventricular systole (aortic ejection wave). A normal mechanical PR interval is <150 ms; values ≥150 ms indicate first-degree AV block.
reference: SMFM Guidance for Performance of a PR Interval; Donofrio et al. AHA 2014

question: Which of the following is a strict documentation requirement for CPT 76826 that distinguishes it from routine obstetric ultrasound freeze-frames?
options: Archiving real-time cine clips of the beating heart across standard segmental views
Documenting maternal heart rate and blood pressure on the ultrasound image
Recording 3D/4D surface rendering of the fetal chest wall
Performing transvaginal color Doppler interrogation in all trimesters
explanation: Both ASE and SMFM standards dictate that static still frames alone are inadequate to evaluate fetal cardiac contractility, valve motion, and rhythm dynamics. Real-time cine loops of the beating heart must be archived in PACS across standard views (4-chamber sweep, LVOT, RVOT, 3VV, 3VT, arches) to support compliant billing of CPT 76826.
reference: ASE Guidelines 2023; ISUOG Fetal Cardiac Screening 2023

question: An MFM physician dictates a routine fetal growth report and inserts the following single sentence: 'Fetal heart 4-chamber view and outflow tracts appear stable with known VSD.' Why does this report fail compliance for CPT 76826 + 76828 + 93325?
options: The sentence is too long for an ultrasound macro
Payers require a discrete, standalone report (or distinct titled section) documenting prior study date, 2D structural sweeps, color mapping, spectral hemodynamics, and interval change
MFM physicians are not legally permitted to bill 76826 without pediatric cardiology co-signature
The report failed to specify the fetal sex
explanation: When cardiac findings are embedded casually inside a general obstetric report without discrete headings, documented Doppler interpretation, prior study reference, and explicit interval change analysis, certified coders are legally constrained to billing 76816. A compliant claim requires an independent, structured cardiovascular report.
reference: SMFM Coding White Paper; ACOG Practice Update 2025

question: According to the American Society of Echocardiography (ASE 2023) and American Heart Association (AHA 2014), what is the recommended serial echocardiography interval for dynamic or progressive lesions (e.g., evolving cardiomyopathy, progressive left-heart obstruction)?
options: Once in the third trimester at 36 weeks
Every 2 to 4 weeks
Every 10 to 12 weeks
Only after birth in the neonatal intensive care unit
explanation: ASE and AHA guidelines recommend serial fetal echocardiograms every 2 to 4 weeks for progressive or dynamic cardiac lesions (such as cardiomyopathy, evolving aortic stenosis, moderate valve regurgitation, or chamber disproportion) to monitor for deterioration, hydrops, or need for urgent delivery planning. Stable lesions may be monitored every 2 to 8 weeks.
reference: Moon-Grady et al. ASE 2023; Donofrio et al. AHA 2014

question: How should a clinical department's EHR order entry system be configured to prevent downstream fetal echocardiography undercoding?
options: Remove all ultrasound orders and use free-text clinical notes
Create a dedicated orderable 'US Fetal Echo Follow-up (76826/76828/93325)' with mandatory baseline complete echo date and target lesion prompts
Instruct schedulers to book all pregnant returns under 'OB Ultrasound Follow-up (76816)' to expedite check-in
Require patients to obtain commercial payer approval prior to scheduling each scan
explanation: Operational alignment starts at scheduling. Creating a distinct EHR orderable ('US Fetal Echo Follow-up') with mandatory prompts (baseline date, performing center, target lesion) ensures the modality worklist tags the study properly, the sonographer executes the full cardiac protocol, the physician uses the correct report template, and billing drops the compliant triad.
